prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Signing in automatically restores your saved desktop pets, customizations, and settings."]
1: ["Initializing desktop overlay engine and loading pet graphics..."]
2: ["Sign In to Reconnect Your Desktop Companion", "Restore Saved Pet Profile"]
3: ["Desktop Pet Quick Controls", "Use Alt+P to summon your pet anytime or right-click the pet to open companion controls.", "Press Alt+P to toggle desktop pet visibility"]
4: ["Analyzing photo features... Clean lighting ensures accurate custom pet generation."]
5: ["Preparing Desktop Overlay", "Testing companion desktop response while final assets build.", "Loading desktop overlay components..."]
6: ["Your pet progress and customization data are automatically synced and safe across sessions."]
7: ["Your Desktop Companion is Ready!", "Try these quick desktop actions to interact with your pet now:", "Right-click pet for companion menu | Alt+H to hide pet"]
8: []
9: ["Desktop overlay loading: Check system tray if your pet does not automatically appear on screen."]
